minutes.headline: Select Board tabled the right of first refusal on 90 West Townsend Road land to research neighboring conservation and Chapter land.
minutes.summary: The board recognized two firefighters, appointed a Conservation Commission member, and ratified two town appointments. It tabled the Chapter 61B right of first refusal on the Pellerini property for more research. Committee reports covered a Town Hall and municipal offices feasibility study and the village district bylaw and public outreach.

what_happened.line: The Select Board tabled the town's Chapter 61B right of first refusal on the 90 West Townsend Road land until more is learned about nearby conservation and Chapter land.
The board appointed Brad Kennedy to the Conservation Commission, and the vote passed.
The board ratified two town staff appointments, an assistant building inspector and a public safety coordinator desk officer, both by passing votes.
The board agreed to work toward criteria for judging neighboring land for future town facility expansion.
The board approved a letter to the governor-elect supporting solar energy, and the town manager is to add a pipeline project information section to the town website.

why_it_matters: Tabling the right of first refusal postpones the town's chance to decide whether to buy the land, and the 61B option has a limited window, so a later decision could be a spending question for the town budget, mostly taxes.
The Town Hall and municipal offices feasibility study, proposed in place of larger engineering funding, could appear as a capital plan item residents are asked to fund.
watch_next: Whether the Select Board returns to the 90 West Townsend Road right of first refusal once information on the neighboring conservation and Chapter land is gathered.
